clue.text: Firm notes on instrument

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places one thing before or atop the next, so the notes come ahead of the instrument

blocks.note: the second note of the sol-fa scale
the fifth note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt soh
a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A firm's musical notes are written for some instrument, or someone plays notes firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' gives two sol-fa syllables in a row, from the do-re-mi scale, and 'on' puts them ahead of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolute person is determined and unwavering, which is a sense of firm.

clue.text: Drivers experience such strange, happy tears

definitions.text: Drivers experience such strange, happy tears

blocks.note: the surface suggests odd tears of joy shed by motorists
the setter means ridged bands on a road that make tyres judder and drone, warning drivers to slow down or stay in lane

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'tears' as rips or strips rather than crying, and 'strange' as the odd noise these road markings make under the wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: These are raised or grooved road markings that vibrate noisily under a car's tyres to alert the motorist.

clue.text: See 1
Laxity is nothing to lose head about

indicators.note: one word goes about, or around, another, so it wraps the empty letter

blocks.note: taken as written
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Slackness is no reason to panic, a soothing bit of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the top of the body, but it is a headland, a sense found in place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity is slackness, a lack of tightness or strictness, which is exactly what looseness describes.

clue.text: Vision of the not too distant future?

blocks.note: first meaning: normal, perfect eyesight measured on a sight chart
second meaning: the year 2020, not far off when the puzzle appeared in 2006

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea, a glimpse of the future, but splits into eyesight and a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal eyesight is scored 20/20 on an eye test, and 2020 was a year only fourteen years ahead of publication.

clue.text: Turn up a very quiet organ

blocks.note: taken as written
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Instruction to raise the volume on a soft church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks musical but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to arrive or show up, and to appear means to come into sight.

clue.text: Palpation is oddly uncomplicated

indicators.note: oddly asks for the characters in positions one, three, five and so on

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A medical examination by touch is strangely straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: Palpation is a doctor feeling the body with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple or without complication, a straightforward synonym for uncomplicated.

clue.text: A number of deliveries

blocks.note: the surface suggests a count of parcels or post
the setter means something that numbs, an anaesthetic used during childbirth deliveries

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'number' as numb-er, a thing that numbs, and 'deliveries' as births.
explanation.definitionFit: This spinal anaesthetic injection is widely used to numb pain during labour and birth.

clue.text: Soldier with explosive behind train

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
high explosive
British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A soldier with a bomb strapped behind a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb, to practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or drill for a performance, the verb sense of train.

clue.text: Chairman prepared to hold marine mammal

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Chairman Mao Zedong, China's leader
Royal Marine
ready, as in all set

explanation.surface: A chairman gets ready to grip a sea creature, apparently a marine mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine mammal' reads as one phrase, a seal or whale; marine is a Royal Marine and mammal stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey, and monkeys are mammals.

clue.text: Little John is hard, but generous

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet, and LAV is short for lavatory
taken as written
the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's big companion Little John is tough but kindhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little John' looks like the outlaw; 'little' signals an abbreviated word for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish describes giving freely and in abundance, which is what a generous person does.

clue.text: Smashed urns — dark load spilt

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered and messed about, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Urns are broken and their dark contents spilled on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' looks like it describes the urns, but it is the definition, slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is slang for heavily intoxicated, and the idiom names someone extremely inebriated.

clue.text: Licks last chocolate drop

indicators.note: last points to the final character of the next word only

blocks.note: laps up with the tongue, as a cat does
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone licks up the last chocolate drop from the bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chocolate drop' looks like one sweet; drop stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a fall or decline, as in a lapse in standards, which is a sense of drop.

clue.text: Creature natural at spinning

indicators.note: spinning turns things round and round, so the preceding letters are whirled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal that is naturally good at spinning, as a spider spins webs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' does double duty here: it joins the fodder and it is part of the spinning phrase; only its letters count in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hairy spider is a creature, and the surface's spinning suits it.

clue.text: They have a lot more than 99

definitions.text: They have a lot more than 99

blocks.clueFragment: They have a lot more than 99
blocks.note: the surface suggests people owning a large number of things, beyond ninety-nine
the setter means people who have lived past ninety-nine birthdays, reaching a hundred or more

explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' suggests possessions, but it means years of life.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people aged a hundred or over, so they have lived beyond ninety-nine years.

clue.text: Bizarre love triangles force out family

indicators.note: forced out means expelled, so that letter leaves the collection
something bizarre is weird and contorted, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a score of zero in tennis
taken as written
the symbol for gravitational force, g

explanation.surface: Strange love triangles drive a family apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love triangles' reads as one phrase; love is O, and the G for force is taken out of triangles before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations are relatives, the members of one's family.

clue.text: Funny bone, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word and listen to how it comes out

blocks.note: the humerus is the upper arm bone, nicknamed the funny bone

explanation.surface: The 'funny bone', so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The funny bone is a nerve at the elbow near the humerus; the pun on that name is the old joke behind the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous means amusing or comic, a plain synonym for funny.

clue.text: Birdman of Alcatraz — first half edited by new monarch

indicators.note: first half asks for only the opening portion of the phrase that precedes it
edited text is altered and reworked, so those letters are reordered

blocks.note: the first five of its ten letters
abbreviation for new
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The film Birdman of Alcatraz, about a convict who kept birds, has been cut and edited for a new king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdman of Alcatraz' is a film title, but only Birdman is the definition; 'of Alcatraz' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer keeps and trains hawks and falcons, so is a man who works with birds.

clue.text: It's conclusive — can't insert key

blocks.note: first meaning: of an argument, impossible to refute
second meaning: in crossword terms, a clue whose solution, the key, cannot be found to write in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key but means the solution to a puzzle, as in an answer key.
explanation.definitionFit: An unanswerable case admits no reply, so it settles the matter; a clue that cannot be answered leaves its solution unwritten.

clue.text: Work out with fish in river

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

blocks.note: a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
a common food fish

explanation.surface: An angler works out with fish in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode is to decipher or figure out a meaning, as you work out a message.

clue.text: Agree that rising oceans contain unknowns

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards
contain means hold inside, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: oceans are seas
y is a mathematical unknown, so two of them

explanation.surface: Agreeing that rising sea levels hold unknown dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to something is to give your consent, to answer in the affirmative.

clue.text: Players almost score

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the ending is cut short

blocks.note: to score a piece of music is to arrange it for instruments

explanation.surface: Some players almost scored, as in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'score' suggest sport, but they are musicians and a musical arrangement; the last two letters are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of instrumental musicians, so it is a group of players.

clue.text: Skim head off ale? That's strange

indicators.note: skimming the head off a drink removes its top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: ale is a beer
i.e., Latin id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: Someone skims the froth from a pint and finds it odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of a beer is its froth, but here it is the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird and unsettling, a spookier shade of strange.

clue.text: Foreign character volunteers for duty?

blocks.note: the definite article, as in the volunteers
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A foreigner volunteers to serve, perhaps signing up for military duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army, the TA, was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, so the volunteers are 'the TA'.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Cantankerous Nero off the rails

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered Emperor Nero has gone off the rails, as in losing his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the rails' reads as one idiom for going mad; 'off' signals the shuffle and 'the rails' is the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornery is American dialect for bad-tempered and contrary, so it means cantankerous.

clue.text: It goes on and on to my distress

definitions.text: It goes on and on to my distress

indicators.note: to distress is to upset and disturb, so the preceding letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the second word of the phrase, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something tedious drags on and on, much to the speaker's distress.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines; the two 'on's with 'to my' are shuffled to make the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is wearisome sameness, something tediously unvaried that seems endless.

clue.text: Children accept credit for plaster

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: seed means offspring or descendants
the abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: Children accept a credit note in exchange for a sticking plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed is a biblical word for offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a levelling layer of plaster or mortar applied over a floor or wall.

clue.text: Greek hero removes head from corpse (Doctor Seuss)

indicators.note: removing the head of a word takes away its opening letter
to doctor is to tamper with or falsify, so those letters are reworked

blocks.note: a corpse is a dead body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek hero beheads a corpse, then a jarring aside names the children's author Dr Seuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Seuss' looks like the author's name, but Doctor is the shuffle signal acting on Seuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, Ulysses to the Romans, is the hero of Homer's Odyssey.
